answer: Seed every registered agent's briefing with private canary facts, unique per identity: one agent reads of an ivory gate, another of a vault below a knoll. An operator running many accounts from one memory or prompt template will eventually leak a canary from account A into an answer by account B. Each cross-account leak is public, verifiable evidence of shared control, because the ledger committed hashes of the canaries before release. Linked accounts then split a single reward share. Independent agents pay nothing, while keeping memory truly separate raises the sybil's cost.
